nws.synopsis: Quiet weather with slightly below normal temperatures through Wednesday and gusty winds over the coastal waters. Warmer and drier weather returns late week, with well-above-normal temperatures and weak to moderate Santa Ana winds for the weekend.
systems: The thermal ridge axis remains over SoCal today, but high clouds will inhibit some of the afternoon peak heating.
The ridge axis slides eastward quickly today as a deepening low off the coast advances towards Northern California.
As this system moves inland this evening and the gradient tightens, gusty onshore winds will develop over the coastal waters, with a Small Craft Advisory currently in place.
Tonight as this low moves in, an deepening marine layer across much of San Diego County will support some localized light rainfall early Wednesday morning for far southern SD County.

nws.aviation: 040530...SCT-BKN clouds around 2000 to 4000 ft MSL will continue to fill into the inland areas of Orange/San Diego and southern Riverside counties. Areas of -DZ/-RA are possible (15-25% chance) for coastal San Diego County through 07-15z Wednesday, most likely in south county, but aren't expected to lead to any decrease in VIS. There is a relatively high likelihood (70+% chance) that CIGs stay above 3000ft for the most part, but dips to 2500-3000 ft MSL are possible, especially in southern SD County where the -DZ/-RA may occur. Lower clouds start to scatter out around 15z Wednesday. Otherwise, VFR conditions prevailing into the afternoon and evening for tomorrow, with a low chance (less than 10 percent) of cigs based around 2000 to 2500 feet returning to the coastal areas of San Diego after 06Z Thursday and through the end of the forecast period.

sites.name: Torrey Pines
sites.note: Ridge soaring in a steady W to WNW sea breeze. SW or NW is cross (soarable but not great); only east is over the back. Rare thermal days (1,200 ft+) are flagged as a Thermal day.

sites.name: Little Black
sites.note: Best post-frontal site in the county. West-facing, so offshore mornings are over the back.

sites.name: Blossom Valley
sites.note: Inland thermal site; often lines up with Elsinore.

sites.name: Elsinore
sites.note: East-facing over the lake; its own animal. Launch in the light air before the switch; the west wind then builds the convergence inland (Perris, Hemet, Soboba). XC wants 7-8k over the range during the switch and the same or more inland.

sites.name: Soboba
sites.note: Flight park on the San Jacinto front.

sites.name: Otay Mesa
sites.note: Near the border; XC goes north and east.

sites.name: Whale's V
sites.note: SW-facing bowl across Otay Lakes Rd from Skydive San Diego. Non-permitted, not an SDHGPA site: coordinate with the DZ, never land at the DZ, no north wind at all. Ridge plus thermal site flying; a few hundred feet over launch is a good day, XC on great days. Under the SAN approach (3,500 ft), not part of the rating. Launch and LZ heights are estimates.

sites.name: Laguna / Horse / Fuzz
sites.note: Convergence sites: Horse faces west, Laguna faces east over the desert, Fuzz is flown on the same convergence. Horse and Laguna are scored on their own and the better one is shown. Horse can also have a glass-off in a light W-SW evening breeze; Laguna has none. The rating only says whether the setup is there; where and when the convergence sits, and the morning winds, are for you to check.

sites.name: Santa Barbara / Ojai
sites.note: Experimental trip area: the Santa Barbara front range (Skyport, EJ Bowl) and Ojai (Chief's Peak), with points along the crest between them. South-facing front range above Santa Barbara; launch sits above the marine layer, so thermals are measured from the slopes at launch height. Sundowners and other real north winds are over the back. The range and a capping inversion near ridge height squeeze onshore S-SE flow (venturi: stronger and gustier at the ridgeline than the models show) but block a north wind aloft when the lapse rate is strong.

sites.name: Owens Valley
sites.note: Experimental trip area. Big-air site: the main launches are Walt's Point (Sierra side) and Paiute and Flynn's (White Mountains side). We look for high days (10,000 ft+) with almost no wind; any real wind sinks it. Advanced pilots only.
